correctness.rationale: For unit-edge opposite-corner routes retaining length a+b, each adjacent swap changes one layer by one, so it cannot cross the excluded value at a failed vertex. Each side condition is an order-convex sublattice under pointwise path minima and maxima. The nonempty intersections are intervals of the rectangular cell-ideal lattice; deleting maximal excess cells and adding minimal missing cells realizes symmetric-difference distance, and every ambient shortest path changes only disagreement cells. This proves convexity and the extremal diameter. The coordinatewise majority ideal supplies the unique median. Feasibility uses the exact interval recurrence with increments {0,1} and terminal layer {a}; empty layers stop the calculation. This works for boundary faults and when no original-length route survives. For the odd-diagonal family, independent EENN/NNEE blocks realize all signs, while the primitive signed excursions have even semilength and Catalan even-part generating function. No assertion applies to longer detours.
